why: All three legs survive the challenge. (1) QUOTE VERBATIM: curl -sL of sub-agents.md line 903, under the heading '### Concurrent subagent limit' (line 901), begins with the quoted sentence character-for-character. The rest of that line does not reverse it: 'Spawning succeeds again when the running count drops below the limit. To change the limit, set CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS to any positive whole number. Sessions with ultracode active are exempt: the limit isn't enforced there. Requires Claude Code v2.1.217 or later.' Line 905 makes the separation the finding depends on explicit: 'Agents that other features run, such as workflow agents and agent team teammates, follow their own limits instead.' (2) CITED LINES ARE ACCURATE: spawner.ts:103 'const DEFAULT_CONCURRENCY = 16'; :136-142 computeEffectiveConcurrency returns Math.max(1, Math.min(ceiling, cpuCores - 2)); :204 'let semaphore = new Semaphore(computeEffectiveConcurrency(DEFAULT_CONCURRENCY))' with :208 rebuilding it from nextRuntime.concurrency. (3) CONSEQUENCE VERIFIED SEPARATELY FROM THE IDENTIFIER, ONE LAYER UP AND DOWN. Down: Semaphore.acquire (:165-186) pushes an over-limit caller onto a queue and rejects only on an aborted signal, and every spawn runs inside semaphore.run at :587 -- so an over-limit spawn blocks, it never fails. Up: all five spawn paths share that one module singleton -- subagent-tool.ts:282, workflow-tool.ts:466, review-tool.ts:304, subtask.ts:84, guardian-runner.ts:57 -- and our own packages/pi-agent-server/README.md:46 documents the scope of 'concurrency' as 'subagent, workflow', i.e. the collapse is already written down on our side. The error string does not exist in source: grep -ra 'Concurrent subagent limit' over packages/ apps/ returns only this sweep's own doc/JSON rows; grep -ra MAX_CONCURRENT over packages/ apps/ returns only marketplace DEFAULT_MAX_CONCURRENT_FETCHES = 2, so no env var (Claude- or NESSY-named) feeds the cap. WRONG-SUBSYSTEM CHECK: two nearby limits that DO fail are not this one -- subagent-tool.ts:150 throws 'parallel tasks cannot exceed N' (DEFAULT_MAX_PARALLEL_TASKS = 100) for the size of ONE call's task array, a per-invocation batch cap; and server-core/src/sessions/live-agent-ceiling.ts refuses with 'live-agent-ceiling-reached' against a memory-derived host-wide runtime bound max(2, RAM/2GiB), evicting idle sessions first. Neither is a per-session count of running subagents, and neither carries the documented threshold or message. WORKFLOW HALF CONFIRMED, NOT ASSUMED: workflows.md:320 reads 'Up to 16 concurrent agents, fewer on machines with limited CPU cores', so both our number and our cpuCores narrowing are exactly the workflow contract -- which is what makes the subagent side (a flat 20, a hard failure, an env var, an ultracode exemption) the part that diverges. NOT AN OWNER DECISION: the nine dated items in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3 are the seatbelt wildcard, the availableModels/isManagedModelAllowed filter placement, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath/listSubkeys and listSessionSummaries -- none touches concurrency. NOT A DELIBERATE PRODUCT DIFFERENCE: nothing here is branding, the corporate gateway or a dropped subscription flow; the parity audit itself lists 'a session subagent limit, a concurrent limit' among the subagent items both closed frontmatter rows under-enumerated (2026-07-25-nessy-claude-parity-audit.md:1653), i.e. a known-open gap.
correctedState: Confirmed with three refinements. (a) The number and the CPU narrowing are not wrong per se -- workflows.md:320 verbatim is 'Up to 16 concurrent agents, fewer on machines with limited CPU cores', so packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/spawner.ts:103 + :136-142 match the WORKFLOW contract exactly. What diverges is that the single module-level semaphore at :204/:208, entered by every spawn at :587, is the only gate for the subagent path too (subagent-tool.ts:282, workflow-tool.ts:466, review-tool.ts:304, subtask.ts:84, guardian-runner.ts:57; scope documented as 'subagent, workflow' in packages/pi-agent-server/README.md:46), where sub-agents.md:903 specifies an independent per-session ceiling of 20 running subagents, a hard `Concurrent subagent limit reached` failure that tells Claude not to retry, a CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS override, and an ultracode exemption -- and sub-agents.md:905 says workflow agents 'follow their own limits instead'. (b) There is a further consequence the finding did not state: sub-agents.md:905 says an in-session /subtask fork 'takes a slot while it runs and is never blocked by the limit', but ours enters the same semaphore via subtask.ts:84, so a user-started /subtask CAN be queued behind a fan-out. (c) Two failing limits exist nearby and must not be mistaken for this one -- subagent-tool.ts:150 'parallel tasks cannot exceed 100' is a per-call task-array cap, and server-core/src/sessions/live-agent-ceiling.ts's 'live-agent-ceiling-reached' is a memory-derived host-wide agent-runtime bound (max(2, RAM/2GiB)) with LRU eviction of idle sessions. No per-session running-subagent count and no env var reader exists (grep -ra over packages/ apps/: 0 source hits for the error string and for MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS).
